market_question: Will Crude Oil (CL) hit (LOW) $40 by end of June?
reasoning: The market-implied 1.1% probability of CL hitting $40 by June 2026 appears far too low given current prices near $60, elevated macro uncertainty, and historical precedent for rapid oil price declines during recessions. Even with a conservative real‑world estimate, the probability is likely in the 5–15% range, offering a large edge on YES.
evidence_points: WTI crude oil currently trades around $60, meaning a drop to $40 requires only a ~33% decline—well within historical one‑year selloffs (e.g., 2014–2015 saw a 40%+ fall in 7 months).
Tariff tensions and an inverted yield curve point to elevated recession risk in 2025–2026, which would sharply curtail oil demand.
OPEC+ has ample spare capacity and a history of price wars when global demand weakens, raising the chance of a supply‑driven overshoot to the downside.
sources_consulted: OPEC+ production and spare capacity reports
